3a5d024984.q: What should you document in an emergency family information security plan when you manage all household finances and bill payments?
3a5d024984.a: Create a shared Google Doc with all critical information your family might need, including access to password vaults, insurance policy details, passport renewal dates, car tab expiration dates, and house maintenance schedules like HVAC filter changes and water softener maintenance. Point the document to passwords, insurance policies and their details, and use automation tools like N8N and SimpleFin to keep financial account information automatically updated in Notion so family members can access current balances and transactions even if you are no longer alive.

87ec5a5377.q: How can you discover unknown financial accounts a family member may have opened decades ago?
87ec5a5377.a: Request statements from all financial institutions and be alert when receiving statements from accounts you do not recognize. 2209a50b93.q: What multi-factor authentication backup plan should you have if your phone is lost or damaged in an emergency?
2209a50b93.a: Use passkeys when possible instead of phone-based multi-factor codes, and add a backup phone number to accounts so your spouse can receive multi-factor tokens. This ensures critical financial and bill-pay accounts remain accessible even if your primary phone with multi-factor codes is no longer available.

594c36ddc9.q: What is SimpleFin and how can it help automate financial account monitoring for family emergency preparedness?
594c36ddc9.a: SimpleFin is a read-only access tool you can connect to online banking accounts to pull down balances and transactions daily. You can set up a script that automatically categorizes and tags transactions with account numbers and pulls them into Notion, creating a centralized shared view of all checking, savings, 401k, and other accounts that updates itself automatically even if you are not alive.
